Hi Elena — great to meet you and thanks for the clear notes. Recap + attachments below, plus a recommended shortlist after testing your sample prompts against our internal eval harness.

Shortlist (fit + tradeoffs):
- redwood-classic-13b (recommended starting point) — best overall safety/cost balance for clinical summarization; strong P95 latency at short sequence lengths.
- redwood-lite-7b-quant (cost-optimized) — lower tokens/sec for long contexts but very economical if you need reserved capacity.
- openlong-30b (high-capability option) — better on succinctness and rare-case recall but incurs higher tail latency and cost.

Redwood-verified performance snapshots (attached CSV + Console links):
- redwood-classic-13b: TPS ~ 48 tokens/sec avg (single GPU profile), p50 latency 85ms, p95 220ms, p99 430ms for 256-token requests.
- redwood-lite-7b-quant: TPS ~ 110 tokens/sec avg, p50 40ms, p95 140ms, p99 280ms for 256-token requests.
- openlong-30b: TPS ~ 18 tokens/sec avg, p50 170ms, p95 480ms, p99 1.2s for 256-token requests.

Notes on your numbers: given your median/95th token lengths, the 95th latency target under 300ms is achievable on redwood-classic-13b for most short requests (<= 512 tokens) with dedicated capacity + KV prefix caching turned on. For the longest 1,800-token requests we'll likely need a different policy: either a trimmed-summary fallback or routing to the high-capacity variant (openlong-30b) for heavy-lift cases.

Quality/regression concerns and evaluation plan:
- We ran your sample prompt set (attached eval_prompt_set_v3.txt) through our eval harness. Key flags:
  - Medication hallucination rate (precision errors on numeric doses) ~ 3.4% on redwood-classic-13b, 2.1% on openlong-30b.
  - Summary hallucination (fabricated events) F1 deltas were within expected ranges but we recommend targeted prompt engineering + few-shot grounding examples.

Recommended next steps (practical):
1) Pilot config: redwood-classic-13b on a 2-GPU dedicated pool with KV prefix caching and short-response streaming enabled. (We can show a cost estimate.)
2) Run a focused regression job using your EHR sample for the two highest-risk prompt types (med lists, discharge summarization). We will output per-prompt metrics and example failure cases.
3) If hallucination rate remains above your threshold, swap critical med-list requests to openlong-30b or a constrained retrieval + generate flow.
4) Review procurement MAP and timeline — I attached a draft (Medsyn_MVP_MAP.pdf).

Attachments: Medsyn_MVP_MAP.pdf, eval_prompt_set_v3.txt, redwood_perf_snapshots_20270208.csv

Links: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/MEDSYN-20270208 (profiles + sample runs)
